title: Ila show for Larry McKinley pays $10
summary: Ridgley, Earl King and Ernie Cato packed the ILA show; he brought ten pieces for $150 and McKinley gave him $10.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But I'm saying, that was an experience I had, and that song, in the same old way, went to be a pretty good seller because I remember, uh, Earl King, Ernie Cato, and myself, we were at the, uh, at the ILA, we paid on the show for Larry McKenna. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And I, uh, what Earl King had, trick bag I guess. Uh-huh. Ernie Cato had mother-in-law. Right. And I had in the same old way. Right. And we packed that joint. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And, uh, Larry McKenna had asked me to do him a favor. So at that time we had to have ten pieces. So, okay, I did him a favor. I brought ten pieces in there for $150. And the place was packed. And he said, if we do anything good, he'll take care of me.

He took care of me. When the thing was over, I got my $150 and he gave me $10. And he had to search through, I mean, one, the desk was full of money, all the drawers were full of money, the box was full, and he gave me $10. Larry McKenna.
